title: lwIP Integration
description: Integrates the lwIP stack for TCP/IP on microcontrollers and bare-metal systems. The zero-copy API keeps RAM use tiny; the stack runs in a single thread or with an OS. It brings real networking to tiny devices.

demo.title: Demo — lwIP Integration

title: DPDK Poll-Mode Drivers
description: Runs poll-mode drivers that bypass the kernel for line-rate packet processing. Cores spin on NIC rings instead of taking interrupts; throughput hits tens of millions of packets per second. It is the standard for fast packet work.

demo.title: Demo — DPDK Poll-Mode Drivers

title: XDP Fast Path
description: Processes packets in the driver with XDP before the kernel stack sees them. eBPF programs drop, forward, or redirect at millions of packets per core. It is the Linux fast path for filtering and load balancing.

demo.title: Demo — XDP Fast Path

title: Zero-Copy RX Rings
description: Receives packets directly into application buffers via DMA rings. No copies between NIC, kernel, and app; the descriptor ring is the contract. It removes the biggest cost in packet processing.

demo.title: Demo — Zero-Copy RX Rings

title: Polling vs Interrupts
description: Chooses polling at high packet rates and interrupts at low ones. Interrupts cost microseconds each — fine at 10k pps, fatal at 10M; NAPI hybrids switch automatically. The crossover is measured, not guessed.

demo.title: Demo — Polling vs Interrupts

title: TCP Offload Engines
description: Offloads TCP segmentation, checksums, and even full stacks to hardware. TSO builds big segments the NIC splits; full TOE runs TCP on the card. Offload frees CPU for application work.

demo.title: Demo — TCP Offload Engines

title: ARP and Neighbor Discovery
description: Implements ARP for IPv4 and ND for IPv6 on bare metal. Address resolution maps IPs to MACs; the stack caches entries and handles gratuitous announcements. No network works without it.

demo.title: Demo — ARP and Neighbor Discovery

title: DHCP Clients
description: Acquires addresses with minimal DHCP clients for diskless and embedded boots. Discover, offer, request, ack — the four-packet dance; leases renew automatically. It is how bare-metal nodes join networks.

demo.title: Demo — DHCP Clients

title: TLS on Bare Metal
description: Runs TLS without an OS using embedded TLS libraries. mbedTLS and wolfSSL do full handshakes in kilobytes of RAM; hardware crypto accelerates the math. Secure bare-metal communication is practical.

demo.title: Demo — TLS on Bare Metal

title: Lock-Free Ring Buffers
description: Passes packets between cores with lock-free rings. Single-producer single-consumer rings need only memory barriers; they are the fastest IPC for packets. DPDK rings are the reference design.
key_mechanisms: Size rings as powers of two

demo.title: Demo — Lock-Free Ring Buffers

title: Receive-Side Scaling
description: Spreads flows across RX queues with RSS hashing so multiple cores share the load. The NIC hashes headers into queue selection; each queue has its own core. It parallelizes receive processing.

demo.title: Demo — Receive-Side Scaling

title: Network Boot Chains
description: Chains network boot from PXE to iPXE to the OS image over HTTP. Each stage fetches the next with more capability; HTTP replaces slow TFTP for big images. Diskless fleets boot this way.

demo.title: Demo — Network Boot Chains

title: Link Negotiation
description: Negotiates link speed and duplex with autonegotiation. Both ends advertise capabilities and pick the best common mode; forced settings are a classic misconfiguration. It just works when left alone.

demo.title: Demo — Link Negotiation

title: BPF Packet Filters
description: Filters packets in the kernel or driver with BPF before userspace wakes. Classic BPF and eBPF programs decide per packet at near-zero cost. Tcpdump made it famous; XDP made it fast.

demo.title: Demo — BPF Packet Filters

title: PTP Time Sync
description: Synchronizes clocks to sub-microsecond with Precision Time Protocol. Hardware timestamping at the PHY removes jitter; the servo disciplines the clock. Trading and telecom need it.

demo.title: Demo — PTP Time Sync
